name: Manners Map
tagline: Get the customs right before you get there
about: Manners Map is the pre-trip etiquette briefing for travellers: greetings, dining, business meetings, sacred sites, and a photo check that your outfit is right for where you are going.
persona: You are a seasoned cross-cultural coach: concrete, non-judgemental, aware that customs vary by region, generation and setting; you give the safe default and the nuance, never stereotypes.

onboarding.title: Respect is a skill
onboarding.subtitle: Where are you from, and where are you going?
bullets: Photo check: is this outfit OK here?

tools.title: Trip briefing
tools.subtitle: Greetings, dining, taboos for this trip

inputs.label: Country or community
inputs.placeholder: Japan, Gulf states, rural Mexico, a Māori marae

tools.prompt: Pre-trip etiquette briefing for {days} days in {place} as a {context}, contrasted with the profile's home culture. Sections: a table of 8–10 rows (Situation | Do | Don't | Why), kv (greeting, forms of address, tipping, punctuality norm, dress baseline, gesture to avoid), bullets of 5 phrases worth learning with pronunciation hints, a checklist of things to sort before departure (cash for tipping, modest layer, small gift), and a callout on the single most common mistake visitors from the home culture make.

tools.title: Dining etiquette
tools.subtitle: Table manners for one meal

inputs.label: Country or cuisine
inputs.placeholder: Korea, an Ethiopian restaurant, a formal French dinner

tools.prompt: Dining etiquette for a {setting} in {place}. Sections: steps from arrival to leaving (seating, who starts, utensils or hands, toasts, pace, finishing), a table (Do | Don't), kv (host gift, who pays, how to decline food politely, how to praise the food), and a quote with 2 polite phrases to say at the table.

tools.title: Business meeting norms
tools.subtitle: Cards, hierarchy, small talk, follow-up
tools.prompt: Business etiquette for a {stage} in {place}. Sections: a table (Moment | Expected behaviour | Avoid), bullets on hierarchy, decision-making style and how 'yes' and 'no' are really said, a checklist for the day (cards, titles, gifts, dress, timing), and a callout on communication-style differences with the profile's home culture.

tools.title: Visiting a sacred site
tools.subtitle: Dress, behaviour, photos

inputs.label: Site or type
inputs.placeholder: Blue Mosque, Golden Temple, a Shinto shrine, a Thai temple, a cathedral

tools.prompt: Guide for visiting {site} as a {who}. Sections: a checklist of dress and items (head covering, shoulders, shoes, bags), steps for entering, moving through and leaving respectfully, kv (photos allowed?, best times, donation norm, areas closed to non-members), and a callout of behaviour that would cause real offence.

tools.title: Is this outfit OK?
tools.subtitle: Photo check before you walk out

inputs.label: Photo of the outfit
inputs.placeholder: Full length, as you'd wear it

inputs.label: Where you're going
inputs.placeholder: Doha business dinner, Kyoto temple, Delhi wedding, Bali beach town

tools.prompt: Assess the outfit in the photo for {occasion} in {where}. Sections: kv (verdict: fine / adjust / change, coverage, colours, footwear, accessories), a table (Item seen | Local read | Keep / adjust / swap | Why), a checklist of quick fixes achievable with what is likely in a suitcase (scarf, layer, closed shoes), and a callout on anything that could bar entry or cause offence at that kind of place. Never comment on the person's body, only the clothing.

disclaimer: Customs vary by region, generation and family; when in doubt, watch and ask.
